s.note: Thick Philly bakery focaccia spread with slow-cooked sweet tomato sauce, served at room temperature with pecorino and oregano
s.how: Mix 400g bread flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, 300ml warm water and 2 tbsp olive oil and rise for 1 hour. Simmer 800g crushed tomatoes with 2 tbsp oil, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano and 1 tsp sugar for 30 minutes. Press the dough into an oiled tray, rest 20 minutes, spread with the sauce and bake at 220C for 25 minutes. Cool to room temperature, dust with 30g grated pecorino and more oregano and cut into squares.

s.note: Mickey's gym reopens on the old block. Roast pork, broccolini and provolone in soft rolls
s.how: Rub 800g pork neck with 4 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp fennel seeds, 1 tbsp chopped rosemary, oil, salt and pepper and roast covered with 250ml chicken stock at 160C for 2 hours. Rest, slice thin and return to the juices. Fry 2 bunches broccolini with 2 garlic cloves and chilli flakes. Fill 8 soft rolls with pork, a slice of provolone each and broccolini, and spoon over the juices.

m.note: Crumbed and fried beef steaks under peppery cream gravy, with buttery mash and green beans
m.how: Boil 800g potatoes and mash with 40g butter and 80ml milk. Pound 4 thin beef steaks (600g), dip in 150g flour seasoned with paprika and garlic powder, then 2 eggs beaten with 125ml milk, then the flour again. Fry in 125ml oil for 3 to 4 minutes a side. Pour off most of the oil, add 30g butter and 2 tbsp flour, whisk in 500ml milk and plenty of black pepper and simmer to a thick gravy. Serve with the mash and 300g steamed green beans.

w.note: Little fried dough balls with lemon and orange zest, tossed in warm honey and piled into a wreath with sprinkles
w.how: Mix 250g plain flour, half a tsp baking powder, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 2 eggs, 30g melted butter and the zest of 1 lemon and 1 orange into a soft dough and rest 30 minutes. Roll into thin ropes and cut into small pieces. Fry at 170C in batches for 2 minutes until golden. Warm 175g honey, toss the balls through, pile into a wreath on a plate and scatter with 2 tbsp sprinkles. Leave to set for 20 minutes.

d.note: An ice-cold lager with a shot of rye whiskey on the side, the way the neighbourhood bars pour it
d.how: Chill 4 beer glasses and 4 shot glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Pour 30ml rye whiskey into each shot glass and serve each next to a 375ml cold lager.
